title: ALMA Observations of the Largest Proto-Planetary Disk in the Orion Nebula, 114-426: A CO Silhouette
question: What are the dust mass, gas tracers and CO kinematics (central star mass) of the largest silhouette disk in the Orion Nebula, 114-426, from ALMA Band 7 data?

data.sensitivity: continuum ~0.56 mJy/beam; line 0.025-0.1 Jy/beam per channel

what.value: Single-dish 12CO J=1-0 background used to estimate background temperature

evidence.quote: The background is estimated by interpolation of the $^{12}$CO emission in the J=1$-$0 emission from (cite: Shimajiri2011)
950 AU at a distance of 414 pc (cite: Menten2007)

recipe.method: Elliptical aperture flux sum divided by N_pix; beam deconvolved sizes

recipe.goal: Derive disk mass from dust continuum
recipe.method: Optically thin M = S D^2/(kappa B(T))
assumptions: kappa=0.034 cm^2/g, gas-to-dust 100, T_dust=20 K, D=414 pc

recipe.goal: Measure CO absorption depths and velocities
recipe.method: Locate deepest absorption per channel; convert Jy/beam to K; compare with interpolated single-dish background
Keplerian from separation and velocity difference of absorption minima; plus thin optically thick Keplerian disk model convolved with beam
key_parameters: free parameters: inner hole radius R_in and M_*
assumptions: edge-on disk, Keplerian rotation, D=414 pc

evidence.quote: Using these values, the disk mass is only 3.1$\pm$0.6 times the mass of Jupiter .
has the strongest CO absorption with a depth of $-$0.63 Jy beam$^{-1}$
differ in radial velocity by $\Delta$V = 2.9 $\pm$0.2 km s$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: Details of the Keplerian CO absorption model fit (likelihood, grid, inclination, parameter ranges)
How the background CO temperature was interpolated per channel
Aperture used for flux measurement beyond its approximate size
score_reason: Public data and simple formulae, but calibration/imaging and the disk model are not specified.
rediscovery_reason: Public data and simple numeric results (flux, mass, absorption depths), though imaging details must come from Mann et al. 2014.
